findings.title: Server-only payment secret read inside a "use client" module
findings.explanation: Checkout.tsx is a client module ("use client" on line 1). Its pay() function reads process.env.PAYMENT_SECRET_KEY, a non-NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable. Next.js does not inline non-prefixed variables into client bundles, so in the browser the Authorization header becomes 'Bearer undefined' and the charge request fails. The secret value is not hard-coded, so nothing leaks as written, but the pattern places a payment credential in client code. If someone renames the variable to NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMENT_SECRET_KEY to make it work, the secret would be shipped to every visitor. Assumption: the variable name denotes a real secret, as its name suggests.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the charge call into a Server Action or Route Handler that reads PAYMENT_SECRET_KEY on the server, and have Checkout call that endpoint with no credential in the browser.

findings.title: Large above-the-fold hero image uses a plain img element
findings.explanation: Hero is the first element rendered by the page (app/page.tsx line 9), so this image is above the fold. A plain gets no automatic sizing, lazy-loading control, modern format conversion or priority hint, which can hurt LCP and cause layout shift. The project depends on next ^14.2.0, so next/image is available. Assumption: the file size is large, inferred from the file name hero-4000x2500.jpg; the actual bytes and dimensions were not inspected.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with next/image: <Image src="/hero-4000x2500.jpg" alt="Mountains at sunrise" width={4000} height={2500} priority /> (or a smaller source with matching width and height).

findings.title: Page file is marked "use client" without using any client-only feature
findings.explanation: app/page.tsx declares "use client" but uses no state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs or context. Its children (Hero and the static posts array from data/posts.ts) are also client-agnostic. The directive forces the page and its data into the client bundle and rules out a server-rendered page that could fetch data on the server. Impact is limited because the data is a small static array.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the "use client" directive so the page renders on the server. Keep the directive only on interactive leaf components.

limitations: No next.config.* file, ESLint config, lockfile or .env file exists in the fixture, so framework config, lint suppressions and environment setup could not be checked.
app/components/Checkout.tsx is not imported by any file in the fixture; it was reviewed as a standalone client module.

Checkout.tsx pay() has no error handling: if the fetch rejects, status stays 'paying' and the button stays disabled. This is a real defect but no reference rule covers it, so it is not reported as a finding.
Hero image size is inferred from the file name only; the file was not inspected. The payment API contract at api.payments.example was not verifiable.
Color contrast, focus appearance and screen-reader output were not assessed, as they cannot be verified from source alone.
No runtime or build verification was performed; the review is source-only and read-only, and no project commands were run.
